reviews.title: Good but getting beat
reviews.text:
I’ve had onX for years. Countless pins and hunts with this app. However, lately competing apps have been doing a better job in my region, updating maps and adding new features like lidar that make it hard to continue justifying the cost of an annual subscription. 

I’m a southern hunter (big game and waterfowl). Hurricane Helene completely changed the landscape in 2024 in some of the land that I hunt. There still hasn’t been a usable map upload that represents the current lay of the land. 

The only reason I use onX now is to compare public/private land boundaries with other apps and reference old pins. 

If you’re considering this app and you’re in the SOUTH EAST go with one of the competitors (Spartan Forge/Huntstand). I’ll be doing the same next season unless there are some drastic changes.

reviews.title: Please update 2D-3D transition!
reviews.text:
I love so much about this app. I have used it religiously this past year hunting elk. But there are some MAJOR quirks that should be ironed out. If you use this like I have, you will understand why these are hellish quirks. When you are in the field in a remote area, no service, and exhausted, trying to traverse some intense backcountry- having the map shift back to its normal position is maddening. Re-opening reorientates the map and it is frustrating ESPECIALLY when you’re hiking 12+ hours.  Why can’t it pick up from the same angle you left it??! 

And the other even MORE annoying and frustrating part is when you are in 3d trying to adjust your angle and go to far it shifts into 2D and force reorients the map as well??? Devs- I beg of you to look into this and fix it. It would be GOLD after that. These issues although somewhat minor, have had a major impact on my overall enjoyment of the other awesome parts of the app.

reviews.title: Be careful
reviews.text:
For all you hunters out there using onX Hunt, be very careful if you’re trusting them. I purchased a 3 acre property last year and I thought by contacting them it would help them out by keeping their information accurate. They won’t update it. Lesson learned, if you’re gonna go hunting and trusting property boundaries don’t trust on X because it could be very old information. I figured they don’t check it every day and it might help them to update them. They said they only update their maps every one to two years based on county records. We all know counties are very slow.  I understand that and figured if someone took the time to reach out to them, they might update the information. But no, they won’t.   In today’s world of digital information where yesterday‘s news is already old news. On x Hunt is still using possibly two-year-old information.
Update:  when I originally contacted them I offered to provide any documentation proving that I was the owner of the property but they didn’t want any of that.  They insisted that they get their information from county records.  Now that I left this review they said if I could provide the information they could update it.  Sure doesn’t seem like they care that much to keeping their records updated until you leave a one star review.
